_comment: nst/JSONTestSuite n_* files that this plugin ACCEPTS in strict mode
(disallowComments: true, no trailing commas) even though RFC 8259 requires
rejecting them. Every entry is an intentional leniency inherited from the
@tabnas/jsonic base grammar that the jsonc plugin does not currently tighten.
This file is OURS (it records our gaps and our reasons). The corpus it
refers to is third-party and is NOT committed — scripts/fetch-conformance-suites.sh
fetches it at a pinned SHA into the gitignored test/vendor/.
This is a PIN, not a skip list. Both ts/test/jsontestsuite.test.ts and
go/jsontestsuite_test.go fail if the set grows (a new leniency appeared) OR
shrinks (a listed leniency was fixed and the pin is now stale). Both runtimes
read this one file, so TS and Go cannot drift apart on it silently either.
Every entry must carry a written reason. Do NOT add an entry to make a run
green: an entry here is an admission of a conformance gap, and each one is a
candidate for a real fix in the grammar.
The unpinned, no-allowlist reading of the dial lives in test/vendor/corpus.json
expected to be red; this pin is only about the strict-JSON mode of the RFC
mode: disallowComments: true (strict JSON), trailing commas off

lenient.n_array_comma_after_close.json: input [""], — jsonic treats the trailing comma at top level as an implicit list continuation instead of an error
lenient.n_number_+1.json: input [+1] — jsonic's number matcher accepts a leading + sign, which RFC 8259 does not allow
lenient.n_number_-01.json: input [-01] — jsonic's number matcher accepts leading zeros
lenient.n_number_-2..json: input [-2.] — jsonic's number matcher accepts a trailing decimal point with no fraction digits
lenient.n_number_0.e1.json: input [0.e1] — jsonic's number matcher accepts a trailing decimal point before the exponent
lenient.n_number_2.e+3.json: input [2.e+3] — trailing decimal point before a signed exponent
lenient.n_number_2.e-3.json: input [2.e-3] — trailing decimal point before a signed exponent
lenient.n_number_2.e3.json: input [2.e3] — trailing decimal point before an exponent
lenient.n_number_neg_int_starting_with_zero.json: input [-012] — leading zeros on a negative integer
lenient.n_number_neg_real_without_int_part.json: input [-.123] — no integer part; the grammar's `exclude` only covers an unsigned leading dot
lenient.n_number_real_without_fractional_part.js: input [1.] — trailing decimal point with no fraction digits
lenient.n_object_non_string_key.json: input {1:1} — jsonic allows a bare number as a map key; RFC 8259 requires a quoted string
lenient.n_object_non_string_key_but_huge_number_: input {9999E9999:1} — bare number as a map key
lenient.n_object_repeated_null_null.json: input {null:null,null:null} — jsonic allows a bare keyword as a map key
lenient.n_single_space.json: input is a single space — the jsonc plugin's #ZZ alt on val.open deliberately resolves a trivia-only document to no value rather than erroring; note the reference implementation (jsonc-parser) reports ValueExpected here, so this leniency is a real divergence from JSONC and not only from RFC 8259
lenient.n_string_escape_x.json: input ["\x00"] — jsonic's string matcher accepts \x hex escapes, which JSON does not define
lenient.n_structure_object_with_trailing_garbage: input {"a": true} "x" — jsonic accepts a second top-level value and silently discards it
